records.name: The Philadelphia Suns
records.summary: A volunteer nonprofit in Chinatown that runs youth basketball and volleyball, a lion dance troupe, a tech team, scholarships and college visits.
records.what_you_do: Young people can take part in basketball, volleyball, lion dance and tech programs. Volunteers help with athletic programs, community service, lion head repairs and leadership roles, and the volunteer page lists roles such as youth basketball assistant coach, event coordinator and graphic designer.

schedule.text: Lion dances at Lunar New Year parades in Chinatown in February, performances booked year-round for events, and youth basketball assistant coaching on Saturday mornings in season.

cost.text: No fees listed. Funded by grants, fundraising and participant contributions.

first_step.how: Fill out the short volunteer survey linked from the Volunteer button on phillysuns.org, or email volunteer@phillysuns.org with questions. Youth coaches also complete onboarding and paperwork.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page gives a short survey and an email address, which is a clear way in. It does not say how a young person joins a team, so it is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: One easy first step is to watch a lion dance at a public event, such as the Lunar New Year parade in Chinatown in February. Volunteer roles run about 5 to 10 hours a month, or 3 hours on Saturday mornings for youth basketball coaches during the season. The site lists no fee to take part, and donations go to programs and scholarships.
first_visit_tips: Ask which clearances a youth coach needs, since the page says only that clearances are required.
Email volunteer@phillysuns.org before you come, since no phone number is listed.
Check the news page for the date of the next Lunar New Year parade.

records.notes: Deep pass: home, get-involved, volunteer, and news pages. The news page shows three dated posts: a Jan 23 post whose title says 2026 (the Lunar New Year parade), a Jul 29 banquet save-the-date whose title says 2026 but whose post shows no year, and a Dec 5, 2025 memorial post. last_sign_of_life stays at 2026-02 (WHYY) because the Jul 29 year is not shown on the page. The site footer reads 2022 and the About Us text is placeholder text, so the site is not fully current. Lion head repairs is carried from tier 1 and is not on the volunteer page. Requirements.background_check is left out because the coaching role says clearances without naming them. Two national tournament bodies named on the site (NACBAIT and NACIVT) are not Philadelphia groups and were dropped. Lion dance booking uses a request form on the site.

records.name: Tribe 12
records.summary: A Jewish social community for people ages 21 to 40 in Philadelphia. Its gatherings include a monthly game night, Shabbat dinners, brunches, and hands-on sessions such as cooking or frame drumming.
records.what_you_do: Pick an event on the calendar, such as game night, a brunch, or a cooking session, and meet other young adults. Some events are free and some have a ticket.

schedule.text: A monthly Game Night on Wednesday evenings and a monthly Shabbat dinner on Friday evenings, plus other events on the events calendar.

cost.text: Some events are free and others are ticketed, with a general price and a higher true cost price that helps keep events accessible. An optional sustainer gift of $12 a month is offered. The group is not a membership organization and lists no dues.

access.notes: Some events are tagged ADA accessible, and events held in private homes may not be physically accessible. ASL interpreters and live captioning (CART) are provided on request if asked for two weeks ahead at info@tribe12.org. The team will discuss lighting or sound on request. Attendees may bring their own items such as earplugs or fidget tools.

first_step.how: Choose a monthly event on the events calendar, such as the Wednesday Game Night, and sign up on its event page. Some events are space limited.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says anyone ages 21 to 40 can join a tribe at any time, that tribes are drop-in, and that people who are just exploring are welcome. It also names a contact form to meet staff.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most calendar entries run about two hours and take place in person, indoors. Some are small, such as the monthly game night at The Board and Brew, which is capped at about 10 people. Some events are free and others are ticketed, and because tribes are drop-in you can come to one event and see how it feels.
first_visit_tips: Check the event page for the exact address, since many calendar entries do not list a venue.
Cancel at least 48 hours ahead for a full refund.
Ask info@tribe12.org at least two weeks ahead if you need an ASL interpreter or live captioning.
Give notice at least 48 hours ahead about food allergies or kosher needs.

records.notes: Deep pass: home, about (FAQ), accessibility, and the events calendar, which lists 20 events from Oct 8 to Nov 12, 2026. Individual event pages (venues and RSVP details) were not opened. Several listed events are free, others have no price shown. Schedule days changed from wed and thu (tier 1, which came from two one-time October events) to wed and fri (the monthly Game Night and monthly Shabbat dinner). kids_ok set to false from the stated 21 to 40 age range. Attendance is allowed through the day of the 41st birthday, so max_age is 40. The site names Board and Brew, the Weitzman Museum and a coffee shop as venues; they are venues, not groups, and were not added to leads.

records.name: United Francisville Civic Association
records.summary: The registered neighborhood group for Francisville. It holds a monthly community meeting, runs monthly trash clean-ups, has a Greening Committee, and follows zoning and development projects in the area.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors hear updates on zoning and development, help with the monthly trash clean-ups (the group provides supplies), and talk over neighborhood plans at the monthly meeting, in person or online.

schedule.text: Monthly community meeting on the second Wednesday, 6:30 to 8 pm, at the Francisville Recreation Center. The Greening Committee meets monthly on Tuesdays at 7 pm at Greenspace in Francisville.

locations.label: Contact address (City list)
locations.address: UFCA, PO Box 56141, 1939 Fairmount Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19130-6141

cost.text: No dues or fees are listed. The group has a donate button, but the site does not say donations are required.

first_step.how: Come to the second Wednesday community meeting at 6:30 pm at the Francisville Recreation Center, 1737 Francis St. The group also offers a virtual option. To ask about events or concerns, email info@ufcaphilly.org.
first_step.basis: The meetings page invites everyone to attend, including residents and business owners, and offers a virtual option. It does not use newcomer language or describe a membership path, so it is rated 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings run from 6:30 to 8 pm, once a month. The group says food and drinks are provided. No agenda was posted on the page we read, and no dues or fees are listed for attending.
first_visit_tips: Read the past meeting minutes posted on the website to see what gets discussed.
The Greening Committee meets on Tuesdays at 7 pm at Greenspace in Francisville, if you want hands-on work.
The group is recruiting volunteers for president, vice president and treasurer, and interested neighbors can say so through a linked folder.

records.notes: Deep pass: home, meetings and committees, and community meetings pages. The FAQ page has no entries on membership, dues, newcomers, age, access or language, so it is not listed as a source. The home page shows the next meeting as Oct 14 without a year; the meetings page gives 2026. The Fall Fest on Oct 24, 2026 at Ogden Park is an event and is not in the schedule. One page offers a virtual option and another lists none; no platform is named. The Zoning Committee and Triangle Lot pages do not say how to join. Meeting minutes are posted by year. The group's mail contact is info@ufcaphilly.org, and the record keeps the City list zoning address in the email field.

records.name: Burholme Community Town Watch and Civic Association
records.summary: A City-registered neighborhood group in the Central Northeast. Its name says it is both a town watch and a civic association, and the City lists it to hear about zoning and development proposals.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over.

first_step.how: Contact the group through the email or phone number on the City list to ask about the next meeting. The only web page we found for the group is a Facebook page, which we did not read.
first_step.basis: No readable public page gives a meeting time, a sign-up step, or a welcome for newcomers. The way in is unclear, so it is rated 2.

records.notes: Deep pass attempted, but the group has no readable own site. Its listed website is a Facebook page, which is a lead-only platform and was not read. One web search returned older Northeast Times coverage and a 2026 author listing that may mention the group. Both Northeast Times pages returned HTTP 403, so nothing from them is recorded. No current meeting time or place could be confirmed, so schedule is left out. The 1128 Cottman Ave address is the City list address and is not confirmed as the meeting place. Status active rests only on the City registration (seen 2026-10-08); no newer dated evidence could be read. Owner may want a human check on this group.

records.name: Fox Chase Civic Association
records.summary: The neighborhood civic group for Fox Chase. It meets monthly with the Fox Chase Town Watch, reviews zoning and building proposals near the neighborhood, and works with local police and elected officials.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come to the monthly meeting to voice concerns, learn what is new, and meet local police and elected officials. Residents can join as dues-paying members, and neighbors can send questions about zoning notices to the group.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the second Wednesday at 7:30 pm at Loudenslager Post 366, 7976 Oxford Ave, held with the Fox Chase Town Watch. There are no meetings in August or December.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: American Legion Loudenslager Post 366, 7976 Oxford Ave., Philadelphia, PA 19111

cost.text: Membership dues are $10 a year. The site lists no fee for attending a meeting.

first_step.how: Come to the second Wednesday meeting at 7:30 pm at Loudenslager Post 366, 7976 Oxford Ave. If you live inside the membership area in the by-laws, you can join as a member for $10 a year.
first_step.basis: Neighbors can attend the open monthly meeting, and membership is a small, clear step. The site does not use newcomer language, so it is rated 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: The monthly meeting is in person at the American Legion post and starts at 7:30 pm, held with the Town Watch. The site says you can voice concerns, learn what is new, and meet local police, state and city representatives. Membership dues are $10 a year and are for residents inside the area set by the by-laws.
first_visit_tips: Check the meeting dates on the home page first, since there are no meetings in August or December.
Watch for orange notices posted outside nearby homes or businesses; they warn of projects that need a zoning variance, and the site explains how to read them.
Confirm the group's email address before you write, since the site lists two different addresses.
Each household can have up to two members.

records.notes: Deep pass: home (2026 meeting dates January to November), membership information ($10 a year; dues period not stated, so not written; two members per household; members from the area in the by-laws), about us (founded in 1992 as a homeowners association, incorporated as a civic association in May 2023), and the zoning page (how to read zoning notice signs). Email conflict: the zoning page's mail link goes to foxchasehomeowners@gmail.com, while the contact field uses foxchasecivic@gmail.com. The tier 1 address is kept, so confirm before publishing. Whether meetings also run online is not stated, so online_ok is left out.

records.name: Rhawnhurst Civic Association
records.summary: The neighborhood civic group for Rhawnhurst. Its monthly meeting brings police community relations reports, updates from elected officials' offices, and talk about local zoning issues.
records.what_you_do: Members attend the monthly meeting, follow local zoning issues, and can help on committees. The group also asks for volunteers to help plan projects, coordinate work, and direct its grant funds.

schedule.text: Regular monthly meeting on the third Wednesday at 7 pm at Pelbano Playground, 8101 Bustleton Avenue.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Pelbano Playground, 8101 Bustleton Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19152

locations.label: Contact address (City list)
locations.address: P.O. Box 11624, 669 Hendrix Street, Phila., Pa 19116

cost.text: Members pay dues to stay in good standing. The amount is not stated on the website; the by-laws or application may list it.

first_step.how: Email Rhawnhurstcivic@aol.com or call 215.439.9074 to ask whether non-members can attend the next monthly meeting, held on the third Wednesday at 7 pm at Pelbano Playground. To join, print the membership application from the website.
first_step.basis: Joining needs a residency check, an application and dues. The site does not say whether non-members can come to meetings, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The meeting is monthly and in person at Pelbano Playground, and the calendar entries run from 7 to 8 pm. The agenda posted for the October 21, 2026 meeting includes police community relations reports, updates from elected officials' offices, and local zoning. Members must pay dues and attend at least three meetings a year to stay in good standing.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the date before you go, since one calendar entry is titled 'March Membership Meeting' but is dated October 21, 2026.
Membership is for residents inside the Rhawnhurst boundary who are at least 18.
Ask whether guests may sit in, since the site does not say.
The page does not say how to return the application, so ask the group before you send it.

The calendar entry is titled 'March Membership Meeting' but is dated Wednesday October 21, 2026, 7 to 8 pm, in person at Pelbano Playground, and the page does not say whether non-members may attend. audience open_to 'public' is carried from tier 1 and needs a human check.
